steps.text: Subtractive synthesis: start with a bright, buzzing wave and take away what you don't want with a filter. Most classic synths work like this. Everything for this lesson is already in the rack.
Patch the voice: SAW of the oscillator to IN of the filter, OUT of the filter to IN 1 of the amplifier, and OUT 1 of the amplifier to jack 1 of the patchbay.
Press Tab and sweep the CUTOFF knob of the filter down and up. Down, the filter takes away the highs and the sound gets dark; up, everything passes.
Turn RESONANCE past the middle. The filter now boosts the frequencies right at the cutoff and starts to sing. Sweep CUTOFF again to hear it.
So far the sound never stops. Press Tab and patch BEAT of the clock to GATE of the envelope. A gate is like a key: high while the key is held down.
Patch ENV of the envelope to CV 1 of the amplifier. The envelope now opens the amplifier on every beat: the drone turns into notes.
Press Tab and turn ATTACK and RELEASE of the envelope. Attack is how fast a note fades in, release how slowly it fades out after the gate ends.
Press Tab and patch a second cable from ENV of the envelope to IN 1 of the scope, to see the envelope's shape.
Press Tab and turn DECAY and SUSTAIN while you watch the scope. After the attack the level falls (decay) to the sustain level and stays there while the gate is high.
One envelope can drive many things. Press Tab and patch another cable from ENV of the envelope to ENV of the filter.
Press Tab and turn up ENV AMOUNT of the filter. Every note now opens the filter and closes it again: the classic synth 'wow'.
Oscillator, filter, amplifier, and an envelope that shapes both the volume and the colour: that is the classic synth voice. Press Next to finish.
